canonical.title: Minimum Time to Burn the Binary Tree
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/06. Min time to burn binary tree.cpp

narrative.title: The Contagion Clock in the Server Farm
narrative.scenario: A corrupted update is detonated on one server blade of a tree-shaped rack network. Each second the corruption jumps to every directly connected blade — the two children and the parent. Ops needs to know the exact second the whole farm goes dark, so they can schedule the isolation window.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and an integer start — the value of the initially infected node. Node values are unique.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of seconds until every node is infected.

testCases.explanation: The fire climbs 8 -> 5 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 6 -> 9 -> 10: seven hops to the farthest blade.
The parent 1 burns first, then the sibling 3 catches it one second later.

hintLevels: Level 1: Fire spreads one ring per second — the answer is the longest escape route from the start node.
Level 2: Convert the tree into an undirected graph by mapping every node to its parent, then BFS outward with a visited set.
Level 3: Each BFS level is one second; when the queue finally empties, the number of completed rings is the burn time.
